paragraphs: Yonatan ben Uzziel: Sukkah 28a and Bava Batra 134a. Hillel had eighty students; the greatest of them was Yonatan ben Uzziel. He translated the Prophets; every bird flying over him was burned. He disputes with Shammai. A man whose son did not behave properly gave Yonatan ben Uzziel his property: there, 133b. Shammai went to him—see his entry—with his staff and bag, saying: ‘Yonatan ben Uzziel has turned the argument against me!’ Shalshelet HaKabbalah 26a writes that he lived long: in youth he received from Haggai, Zekharyah, and Malakhi, and in old age was among Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai’s colleagues; he saw Onkelos the convert, Zohar, Acharei Mot, at the locator עקל״א. But it does not mention Yonatan ben Uzziel there, only Onkelos; see there. Tosafot, Shabbat 115a, write that the translation of the Writings was made in the tannaim’s days, but not by Yonatan, against those saying Rav Yosef made it. So too Tosafot on Megillah 21b (cited here as chapter 1). We do not know who composed the Writings’ translation. Yuchasin, sequence of tannaim, letter gimel under Rabban Gamliel of Yavneh, writes that Yonatan ben Uzziel wrote it. The heavenly voice, ‘Who is this revealing Torah’s secrets?’ came forth when he wished to explain ‘And a redeemer shall come to Zion’; some say the passage ‘The Lord reigns’ (Shalshelet HaKabbalah there). He was buried in the village of Amukkah near Safed. See the margin of Zohar, Pinchas 94a, Sulzbach edition. So too גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]. Another righteous man named Mukrat is there, with a monument over him.
